sections.history: Tirucherai lies near Kudavasal, in Thanjavur district (some sources Tiruvarur), in the Kumbakonam country. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar and Appar, and counted the 95th shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later. (The Shiva temple here is distinct from the Saranatha Perumal Vishnu Divya Desam of the same town.)
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Saara Parameswarar — Gnanaparameswarar, also Senneriyappar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Gnanavalli (Gnanambikai) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. Near the Vinayakar stands a separate lingam, the Rnavimochana Lingeswarar, installed by sage Markandeya, worshipped for release from debt.
sections.legends: The sage Markandeya, by tradition, felt his past karmas lifted on coming here, and installed the Rnavimochana Lingeswarar — 'the lord who looses debt' — beside the Vinayakar; the shrine is especially sought by those seeking relief from debt. Shiva is worshipped as Saara Parameswarar, 'the supreme essence,' with Gnanavalli, 'she of wisdom,' beside him. The fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), the Annabishekam in Aippasi (October–November), Tiruvadhirai in Margazhi (December–January), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Devotees come especially to pray for release from debt.
sections.experience: At Tirucherai the pilgrim comes to the lord of the supreme essence. Before Saara Parameswarar and Gnanavalli, and the Rnavimochana lingam of Markandeya, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple of the Kumbakonam delta, and the hope of release from the burden of debt.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirucherai lies near Kudavasal, roughly midway between Kumbakonam and Nannilam, in Thanjavur district. Kumbakonam is the nearest town and rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
